title: Overview
text:
Target Reaper DevDocs Build less clutter. Keep the work that matters. Target Reaper finds stale Rust targets, generated artifacts and old Git/JJ workspaces. It separates discovery from authorization, starts with a preview, and checks filesystem and process activity again before deleting eligible data. Your first run target-reaper --root "$HOME/src" --age-days 7 --min-size 100M --list
 Start with one projects directory. Read the classifications and retained reasons. Add `--execute` only after reviewing the exact scope and policy you selected. Follow a path I want to… Read Install on a Mac or Linux machine [Installation](install.md) Choose a cleanup scope [Usage](usage.md) Understand what may be deleted [Safety and authorization](safety.md) Look up a flag or exit code [CLI reference](cli.md) Understand the code [Architecture](architecture.md) Build, test or contribute [Development](development.md) Produce a platform-specific binary [Release packaging](releases.md) Schedule a reviewed command [Automation](automation.md) Two native platforms macOS and Linux share the cleanup policies. Native filesystem handles and process snapshots supply platform-specific evidence. GNU `timeout` and Git are required; JJ workspace cleanup additionally uses native `jj`. See [platforms and verification status](platforms.md) before treating a build or historic test result as current runtime evidence. Know the boundary The default policy protects unfinished work. Broader deletion flags grant explicit authority. A preview can become stale, and execution is not atomic against hostile concurrent writers. Reported bytes are logical sizes, not physical free-space measurements. Read the [safety guide](safety.md) before automating a command.

title: Installation
text:
Installation Build Target Reaper natively on the platform where you will run it. The primary packaging targets are Apple-silicon macOS and x86-64 Linux. Requirements Tool Purpose Rust 1.99.1 through rustup Compiler pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml` C toolchain/linker Native dependencies and final linking Git Repository/worktree operations and fixtures GNU `timeout` Bounded external commands Native `jj`, for JJ cleanup Workspace inspection and exact-name operations Use the pinned compiler. Do not set `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP` or remove the wrapper to work around build failures. macOS Install Apple's command-line tools if missing. With Homebrew available: brew install git coreutils
brew install jj # optional unless you use JJ workspace cleanup
export PATH="$(brew --prefix coreutils)/libexec/gnubin:$PATH"
timeout --version
git --version
jj --version # when JJ support is required
 Homebrew supplies GNU `timeout` as `gtimeout` and inside its `gnubin` directory. Derive the actual prefix with `brew --prefix coreutils`; Apple-silicon and Intel Homebrew installations use different prefixes. Mac cleanup uses native `lsof`, mount information and descriptor-relative filesystem operations. Required capability evidence must be available and complete before eligible cleanup proceeds. Linux Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential git coreutils pkg-config
 Arch Linux: sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel git coreutils pkgconf
 Install native `jj` if needed. Verify that `timeout --version` identifies GNU coreutils. Linux process/filesystem checks depend on the native kernel and visible process information. Compile the checkout The current Mac compatibility corrections are on `fix/macos-main-8e73fe0`, based on `main` at `8e73fe0`, pending integration. Use that branch for the verified development snapshot. git clone --branch fix/macos-main-8e73fe0 https://github.com/lprior-repo/target-reaper.git
cd target-reaper
rustup show active-toolchain
cargo build --release --locked
./target/release/target-reaper --version
 The source repository is private. Clone and release downloads require an authorized account; access to public documentation does not grant source access. Install for your user cargo install --path . --locked
command -v target-reaper
target-reaper --version
 Ensure Cargo's bin directory is on your `PATH`. Installing the binary does not schedule cleanup. Review a narrow preview before using execution or [automation](automation.md). Archives Choose the archive matching your OS/architecture, check its SHA-256 manifest, and inspect its build provenance. See [release packaging](releases.md). An archive's existence does not prove that native tests passed for its commit.

title: Mac & Linux
text: Platforms and verification Target Reaper supports native Linux and macOS. Other operating systems are rejected at compile time. Packaging targets OS / architecture Rust target Scope Apple-silicon macOS `aarch64-apple-darwin` Primary Mac package x86-64 Linux, glibc `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` Primary Linux package Intel macOS `x86_64-apple-darwin` Source build; separate native verification required Other Linux architectures Platform-specific target Source build; separate native verification required Windows — Unsupported Every archive identifies its exact target and commit. macOS and Linux binaries are not interchangeable; glibc and musl Linux targets are also distinct. Native capability boundary Capability macOS Linux Process/file activity Native `lsof` snapshots Visible `/proc` process data Mount boundaries Mount snapshots and filesystem identity Kernel/filesystem identity checks Path traversal Descriptor-relative no-follow traversal `openat2` resolution restrictions External command bounds GNU `timeout` via coreutils GNU `timeout` via coreutils Workspace authorization Shared policy, native Git/JJ integration Shared policy, native Git/JJ integration Missing or incomplete required evidence retains candidates. These checks do not create an atomic lock against hostile concurrent writers. Interpreting evidence A native build proves compilation for its target and configuration. A native fixture pass applies to its exact commit, test selection and environment. Cross-compilation or Linux-target Clippy on a Mac is static evidence, not a Linux runtime pass. Older commits' tests remain older-commit evidence until the new head is checked. Empty check lists, interrupted runs and zero-test filters are not passing suites. Current development snapshot This documentation starts from `main` commit `8e73fe0`. Its stable compiler pin exposed a nightly-only wrapper option. The focused compatibility fix supports stable builds while preserving the exact nightly/dev allowlist and rejecting bootstrap overrides. The corrected snapshot passed **1,022 native macOS tests, zero skipped**, on Apple silicon with Rust 1.99.1 and macOS 27.0.1. That run used the `8e73fe0` base plus the reviewed portability fixes. The first complete run had 999 passes and 21 failures; those failures and the resource-stopped build attempts remain preserved. Corrections distinguish an empty test process index from unavailable visibility, use filesystem-portable raw-reference fixtures, and test native path limits explicitly. Production Mac activity checks remain fail closed. Debug symbols and incremental output were disabled for resource containment; runtime assertions and overflow behavior remained unchanged. The initial strict native Clippy run stopped at a 1 GiB task-owned build-cache limit. Its approved 1.5 GiB continuation completed within the limits and reported 14 source errors, prompting the follow-up fixes. Neither failure is recorded as a pass; the earlier test evidence remains tied to its source snapshot. Native macOS ARM64 and Linux x86-64 verification now uses explicitly authorized GitHub-hosted OS runners. The first hosted attempt failed before completing either suite; its receipts remain separate from successful runs. Consult [PR #3 verification](https://github.com/lprior-repo/target-reaper/pull/3/checks) for the latest exact-head result. A skipped, failed or interrupted job is not a current-branch pass. The [release guide](releases.md) describes the resource limits and development-artifact boundary. OS support policy, packaging, and a particular native verification receipt are different facts. See [development](development.md) for the exact verification commands and [release packaging](releases.md) for artifact provenance.

title: Common workflows
text:
Usage Choose a scope, preview it, then authorize execution deliberately. Whole Cargo targets target-reaper --root "$HOME/src" --age-days 7 --min-size 100M --list
 A candidate must be old enough, large enough, inactive and free of protected data. The default `--cargo-only=true` requires a sibling Cargo manifest. Fuzz targets are skipped unless explicitly included. Use `--verbose` for classifications and skipped candidates. Add `--require-clean-scan` when target scan errors should prevent target deletion. Mixed-age build directories target-reaper --root "$HOME/src" --prune-target-files --age-days 7 --list
 This narrower policy can remove recognized old compiler outputs while preserving fresh files and durable data. It does not make an arbitrary target subtree disposable. Generated fuzz and mutation artifacts target-reaper --artifact-root "$HOME/src" --age-days 1 --list
 Generated `fuzz/{corpus,artifacts,crashes,coverage,target}`, `mutants.out`, `mutants.out.old` and `.cargo/mutants` trees are recognized. Harness source is preserved. A fixed 24-hour floor applies even when the global age is zero. Cache entries target-reaper --cache-root "$HOME/.cache/my-builds" --age-days 7 --list
 This inspects immediate child directories with durable-data protections. Cache scope does not authorize deleting arbitrary old database segments or backup receipts. Git worktrees target-reaper --worktree-repo "$HOME/src/project" --age-days 7 --list
target-reaper --worktree-root "$HOME/src" --age-days 7 --list
 The default policy requires clean, integrated, inactive work. A registration may point outside the discovery directory. Primary repositories and shared stores remain protected. Missing registrations and integrated branches require separate opt-ins. Read [the authorization rules](safety.md) before using them. Explicit per-file scope target-reaper --prune-root "$HOME/.cache/disposable-build-output" --age-days 7 --list
 `--prune-root` is broader authority. Old receipts, backups and other files inside that exact directory may be eligible. Point it only at data you mean to make disposable. Execute a reviewed scope Repeat the reviewed command with `--execute`, for example: target-reaper --root "$HOME/src" --age-days 7 --min-size 100M --execute --list
 Execution rechecks live metadata and activity. Preview output is not a saved transaction. `--discard-stale-workspaces` permits irreversible loss of old unfinished work and is not implied by target cleanup. Logs and byte counts `--log PATH` appends category counters and retained reasons, even during preview. Whole targets, physical workspaces, missing registrations and branches have distinct counters. Do not sum overlapping preview estimates. Reported bytes are logical file lengths. Physical reclamation requires an independent filesystem measurement.

title: CLI reference
text:
CLI reference Flags, defaults and exit codes for the current development version. For executable help, run `target-reaper --help`. Flags Flag Short Argument Default Description `--root` `-r` `DIR` (repeatable) *none* Root directories to scan for Cargo targets. Repeat for multiple roots. `--cache-root` — `DIR` (repeatable) *none* Inspect immediate child directories as cache entries. Set roots such as `~/.cache` or `/cache` explicitly. `--prune-root` — `DIR` (repeatable) *none* Explicitly authorize per-file age cleanup inside a specific directory. Recent files, excluded paths, and busy roots are retained. Missing roots are skipped. `--artifact-root` — `DIR` (repeatable) *none* Discover generated `fuzz/{corpus,artifacts,crashes,coverage,target}`, `mutants.out`, and `.cargo/mutants` trees beneath this directory. Contents must be strictly older than 24 hours, even when `--age-days 0`. `--prune-target-files` — — `false` Reclaim old generated compiler artifacts in discovered Cargo targets, including mixed-age targets. Requires `--root`; preserves source and durable fixture/database/evidence subtrees. `--worktree-repo` — `REPO` (repeatable) *none* Inspect worktrees registered to this Git repository. Default policy requires clean, integrated work; primary repositories are always retained. `--worktree-root` — `DIR` (repeatable) *none* Discover Git repositories recursively and inspect their registered worktrees. Discard mode also discovers JJ workspaces. Overlapping routes are deduplicated. `--discard-stale-workspaces` — — `false` Authorize deletion of inactive old Git/JJ checkouts despite dirty, untracked, ignored, unmerged or recovery-bearing contents. Requires a worktree scope; preserves primary repositories and shared stores. `--prune-merged-branches` — — `false` Remove old integrated local Git branches or forget matching local JJ bookmarks. Requires a worktree scope and `--refresh-worktree-defaults`; never deletes remote refs. `--prune-missing-worktrees` — — `false` Remove old missing registrations after validating private metadata. Default policy also requires integrated recovery state; discard mode authorizes its loss. Locked missing registrations remain protected. Requires a worktree scope. `--allow-generated-worktree-cache` — — `false` Permit only verified ignored Moon cache/toolchain outputs in otherwise eligible worktrees. Requires a worktree scope. `--refresh-worktree-defaults` — — `false` Verify authoritative origin main/master. Execution may fetch the selected tracking ref; preview never fetches. Requires a worktree scope. `--worktree-min-size` — `SIZE` `0` Independent minimum size for physical worktrees. Branches and missing registrations have no byte threshold. `--exclude` — `DIR` (repeatable) protected-path defaults Additional paths excluded from target, cache, worktree, and per-file cleanup. `--age-days` `-a` `DAYS` `1` Minimum age in 24-hour periods. Whole targets/caches are retained if recent; pruning evaluates each file independently. `--min-size` `-m` `SIZE` `10MB` Minimum size for whole targets/cache directories. Accepts `100M`, `1.5GB`, `2TB`, `500K`, `1048576` (raw bytes). Worktrees use `--worktree-min-size`; per-file pruning does not use either threshold. `--execute` `-e` — `false` Actually delete. Without this, runs in **dry-run mode**. `--verbose` `-v` — `false` Print every scanned target with its classification. `--list` — — `false` Print stale target paths. Dry-run and execute default to summary-only output. `--quiet` — — `false` Suppress optional per-target output. Prints only the final summary. `--jobs` — `N` `2x CPUs`, capped at 32 Classification worker threads; maximum 128. Useful for I/O-bound metadata scans. `--delete-jobs` — `N` `--jobs` Safe recursive deletion Rayon threads; maximum 128. `--queue` — `N` `4096` Bounded pipeline queue capacity; maximum 65536. `--cargo-only` — `bool` `true` Only include Cargo project targets. Use `--cargo-only=false` for every directory named `target`. `--require-clean-scan` — — `false` A target scan/classification error prevents target deletion. Other cleanup categories use their own checks. `--skip-fuzz` — `bool` `true` Skip `fuzz/target/` directories. Use `--skip-fuzz=false` to include them. `--log` — `PATH` *none* Append numeric cleanup counters and retained reasons, plus the string `workspace_policy`, after completion. Creates parent directories automatically. `--lock-path` — `PATH` Linux: `/run/user/{uid}/target-reaper.lock`; macOS: `/private/tmp/target-reaper-{uid}.lock` Override the shared advisory lock path. Use the same path for automation and manual invocations. `--help` `-h` — — Print help (short form) with examples. `--version` `-V` — — Print version. Exit Codes Code Meaning `0` Success — no errors during scan or deletion `1` Generic error — bad root path, I/O failure, deletion failure `2` Lock held — another `target-reaper` is running, or bad CLI arguments `3` Errors during classification — some targets could not be evaluated Size Format The `--min-size` flag accepts human-readable sizes. All values are case-insensitive. Input Bytes `500`, `500B`, `500b` 500 `10K`, `10KB` 10,240 `100M`, `100MB` 104,857,600 `1.5G`, `1.5GB` 1,610,612,736 `2T`, `2TB` 2,199,023,255,552 `1048576` 1,048,576 (raw bytes) `0.5MB` 524,288 (fractional) Arg Inference Long flags can be abbreviated to their shortest unambiguous prefix: target-reaper -r ~/src --exec     # → --execute
target-reaper -r ~/src --age 7    # → --age-days
target-reaper -r ~/src --min 10M  # → --min-size
 Lock paths The lock serializes cooperating runs. Use one consistent `--lock-path` for manual and scheduled runs. A dry run still acquires this operational lock.

title: Safety & authorization
text: Safety and authorization Start with a narrow root and review a preview before enabling execution. Target Reaper cannot recover deleted data or provide atomic protection against hostile concurrent writers. Each target scan captures one timestamp, one age cutoff, and one process snapshot covering visible executables, working directories, open files and mapped files. Linux uses `/proc` and `openat2`. macOS uses native `lsof` and `mount` capabilities plus descriptor-relative no-follow traversal, device/mount checks and descriptor path revalidation. macOS protects other processes working inside a project as well as identified Cargo workspace ancestors. Missing tools, warnings, incomplete snapshots and ambiguous native path output fail closed; macOS retries incomplete process snapshots at most three times. Its directory reads may update access times because macOS lacks Linux’s per-open `O_NOATIME`. Native path bytes and kernel-escaped map paths are preserved. Preview and execution apply these activity guards; execution takes a fresh snapshot before revalidating targets. A target is stale iff its strict scan observes no regular file under that target with `mtime >= cutoff`. The age cutoff stays fixed throughout a pass. Metadata newer than the scan start is checked against the time it is observed: ordinary writes during a scan are fresh, not clock skew. Genuinely future-dated metadata still fails closed. The library's `scan_roots` result carries this boundary in `ScanResult.cutoff`. Both `delete_stale` and `delete_stale_with_config` preserve it while refreshing process and mount activity. A later configuration may tighten the age boundary but cannot advance it. Library callers constructing `ScanResult` directly must supply the cutoff used to authorize staleness. Traversal errors are not swallowed. Errors are recorded in the scan result and the CLI exits with code `3`. By default, independently proven-stale targets may still be deleted when `--execute` is used. Add `--require-clean-scan` when you want the stronger policy: any target scan/classification error prevents target deletion. Cache and worktree cleanup use their own conservative checks and report command or traversal failures. Git discovery permits at most 10,000,000 raw filesystem entries and 2,000,000 directory checks per root, with depth 128. Ordinary files consume the raw budget but not the directory-check budget. Cache/worktree measurement is limited to 256 levels and 2,000,000 entries; Cargo discovery and target scans to 256 levels and 10,000,000 entries. Per-file plans cap entries at 10,000,000 and directories at 1,000,000. Library walkers cap open directories at 16 each. Discovery-budget failures identify the offending path; exhausted limits fail closed rather than silently authorizing an incomplete tree. Sorted walkers can buffer wide directories, so these are not strict heap-memory guarantees. Cache and Worktree Rules Cache cleanup examines only immediate child directories of each explicitly supplied `--cache-root`. It keeps protected personal/model/Steam paths, non-owned data, symlinks, recent trees, and trees referenced by a visible process. On Linux, individual `/proc` entries that cannot be inspected are ignored; if `/proc` itself is unavailable, cleanup fails closed. On macOS, unavailable or incomplete native process/mount capabilities retain candidates. Process visibility is best-effort and can change after the check. Worktree cleanup accepts `--worktree-repo`, `--worktree-root`, or both. Discovery does not follow symlinks or enter Git/JJ metadata or build payloads. Repositories are deduplicated by their canonical common Git directory; supplying a linked checkout never changes which registration is primary. Protected primary or shared-metadata namespaces retain the repository's worktrees, including registrations outside discovery roots. Discovery prunes conventional SDK/package directories (`.cargo`, `.rustup`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `CMakeFiles`) and recognized Cargo output payloads. A verified native Git root overrides a generated directory name; an empty or bogus `.git` marker does not. Custom output is recognized by a regular `.rustc_info.json` or a `.fingerprint` directory plus a regular Cargo lock marker. `Cargo.toml` and `.jj` markers prevent structural output classification. Hidden directories, `.cache`, and `.codex` are not blanket-excluded; unrecognized payloads remain subject to the explicit traversal limits. Integration uses verified `main` or `master`, never a feature-named `origin/HEAD`. With `--refresh-worktree-defaults`, origin is checked online. Preview retains a repository as `needs_fetch` when local proof is unavailable; execution fetches only the selected tracking ref with an empty refmap, without `--force`, tags, submodules, maintenance or `FETCH_HEAD` replacement. Offline, changed or unverifiable bases are retained. An absent cached `origin/HEAD` permits normal local fallback. An explicitly untrusted cached target or invalid/unsupported remote advertisement retains only that repository without blocking unrelated repositories; unexpected native-invocation and I/O errors still propagate. Under the default **integrated-only** policy, primary, locked, JJ, bare, unborn, protected, recently modified, dirty, unmerged, or process-referenced worktrees are kept. A detached worktree is eligible only when its committed HEAD is an ancestor of the verified integration base. Missing registrations require the separate opt-in below. Under that default policy, untracked or ignored files normally keep a worktree, including Cargo `target/` directories, and artifact cleanup runs first. `--allow-generated-worktree-cache` permits only ignored `.moon/cache/` with a valid `CACHEDIR.TAG` plus inert `tools/build-toolchain.json` identifying that exact checkout and the expected tool fingerprint. Unknown ignored data stays protected. A symlink's own timestamp contributes to activity checks; its target is not followed or counted. Default cleanup refreshes Git identity, registration and HEAD before native `git worktree remove` without `--force`; source repositories and JJ stores are not purged. Default cleanup also verifies the linked checkout's private Git directory. Absolute and relative native Git backpointers are resolved exactly, without traversing symlinks or interpreting a parent traversal through a missing prefix. Recent or process-referenced metadata, unintegrated recovery revisions, hidden index state, unknown files and unverifiable pointers retain the checkout. A fresh complete private snapshot must match the authorization immediately before removal. Preview and execution both check visible activity. Execution repeats eligibility checks; process activity can change after any check. The default policy retains worktrees with `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` index entries, which can hide uncommitted changes. It reads native `git ls-files -v -z` output and never rewrites those flags. Explicit discard authorization permits loss of these hidden changes. `--execute` applies to every explicitly enabled policy. Without it, targets, caches, files, worktrees, registrations and branches are preview-only. Documents, Downloads, Steam, model directories, evidence, backups, snapshots, and project `var/` trees are protected during root scans. Whole-directory deletion uses safe recursive deletion (`remove_dir_all`). Per-file pruning uses descriptor-relative filesystem operations and revalidates entries before unlinking them. Age-Authorized Workspace Discard `--discard-stale-workspaces --age-days 1` requires every observed file, directory and symlink in the checkout, private Git metadata and local JJ metadata to have `mtime` strictly older than one fixed 24-hour cutoff. Commit dates and access times do not authorize removal. Directory timestamps count, so recent deletions or renames keep a checkout. Fresh snapshots include inode, device, mode and change time to detect intervening mutations. Discard runs before target/cache/per-file cleanup so its own artifact deletion cannot make an otherwise old checkout appear newly active. Target roots are validated before any discard; an explicitly supplied target root removed by that authorized pass is consumed rather than reported as an invalid root afterward. Physical ownership, activity, protection and age rejection runs before expensive JJ lease preparation. These rejection reasons take precedence over JJ classification. Eligible removals still repeat the complete activity snapshot and fresh JJ alias/membership checks immediately before mutation; this ordering does not cache away the final safety checks. Planning refreshes known JJ markers and relevant native store memberships without repeating the whole-scope alias walk for each candidate. Before every actual removal, the final guard still repeats scoped alias discovery for metadata-owning candidates. A new alias appearing after initial discovery may therefore change a preview candidate into retained execution state. Primary Git/JJ roots, nested or shared stores, metadata owners referenced by another workspace, protected personal/model/excluded paths, foreign ownership, mounts and visible process references keep a checkout. Discovery does not follow symlink roots. Scoped JJ aliases and native memberships are verified again before removal; unknown or unsupported identity/registry state is retained. Protections cannot discover arbitrary aliases outside the supplied scopes. Ordinary Rust `src/model` and `src/models` module directories do not count as model-weight collections merely because of their name. Only directories and regular `.rs` files qualify for this source-module classification; non-source payloads such as `weights.bin`, symlinks and other protected prefix/suffix namespaces still retain the whole checkout. Protected checkout-root namespaces are unchanged. Present locked Git worktrees may be removed using native double-force removal only after all discard guards pass. Missing locked registrations are retained. Missing Git registrations still require `--prune-missing-worktrees`, an old verified private directory and fresh absence/identity/activity checks. True JJ workspaces use native JSON names and commit IDs, verified store ownership, and an exact snapshot of the authoritative workspace registry. The physical checkout is removed first, then its exact native workspace name is forgotten only after revalidating surviving membership and the registry. If that second step fails, the command exits nonzero and explicitly reports that physical deletion already happened; it does not pretend the operation was rolled back. Preview does not create missing legacy registry files. After a physical-removal/forget failure, fix the underlying lock or repository problem and use native exact-name `jj workspace forget` from the surviving anchor when required. Rerunning the cleaner alone does not automatically repair missing JJ registrations. These are bounded, fail-closed checks, not atomic protection against hostile concurrent writers or a promise that unfinished work is recoverable. No service is stopped. Branch deletion remains a separate, merged-only policy even when workspace discard is enabled. Merged Branches and Missing Registrations `--prune-merged-branches` requires both a worktree scope and `--refresh-worktree-defaults`. Only branch tips strictly older than the fixed cutoff and integrated into the pinned main/master are eligible. Defaults, checked-out branches, and commits/parents owned by any scoped JJ workspace are protected. Every scoped repository's current worktree membership is refreshed before application; unreadable JJ state retains branches. Ordinary Git branches use `git branch -d`, never forced deletion. The verified main/master may temporarily become the branch-specific upstream; failed or retained deletion restores the original tracking values. JJ primaries use exact-name `jj bookmark forget`, not bookmark deletion or push, so this does not schedule remote deletion. Under the default policy, `--prune-missing-worktrees` uses selective native removal, never blanket `git worktree prune`. It requires an old, trustworthy private Git directory, integrated HEAD and HEAD reflog revisions, and no staged index differences. Optional `ORIG_HEAD` must name an actual integrated commit, not a tag or other object. An empty native `refs` directory is allowed; any contained private refs, unknown files, unique recovery state, or changed registration/index/reflog/absence retain the registration. The full private snapshot is checked again before removal. Discard mode changes recovery authorization, not primary/store/age/identity/activity protections. Reports separate physical Git worktrees, JJ workspaces and their logical bytes from missing registrations and branch counts. `--log` includes `workspace_policy=integrated-only` or `workspace_policy=discard-stale`, numeric `worktrees_*`, `jj_workspaces_*`, `stale_worktrees_*` and `branches_*` counters, and fixed category-specific `*_retained_REASON` counters, including zero values. Reasons remain available with `--quiet`. Ordering and decisions are deterministic for the same mode, configuration and filesystem/Git/JJ/process/remote snapshot. Preview is not a saved execution plan and does not simulate earlier removals: execution can release a branch by first removing its eligible worktree. Native commands have a 60-second timeout plus a 5-second kill grace. Captured output is rejected above 64 MiB after capture; this is not a peak-memory guarantee. Visible-process checks and final metadata revalidation do not make hostile concurrent mutations atomic. Preview does not simulate whole-checkout removal: a nested old target can appear in both target and worktree estimates. Do not sum overlapping preview category bytes. Execution counts the actual removal once; an unchanged replay removes nothing further. Explicit Per-File Pruning `--prune-root` captures one cutoff at the start of its pruning pass. Only files with `mtime < cutoff` are eligible; directory timestamps do not make their old contents fresh. Roots and directory entries are ordered deterministically, and duplicate/overlapping roots are counted once. The listing is a preview, not a saved deletion plan: execution rechecks the filesystem and can retain changed or busy roots. The mode keeps the protections for personal files, Steam, models, source checkouts, excluded paths, foreign ownership, and mounted filesystems. It refuses symlink roots and never follows symlink entries into their targets. Explicit roots may contain offline evidence, receipts, and backups that broad scans otherwise preserve. Any detected executable, working directory, open file, or mapped file under a pruning root keeps the **entire root**, including its old files. This avoids deleting an old database segment while its owner is still running. No service is stopped. Process visibility is best-effort; inaccessible process details and a process starting after a check remain limitations. Execution can temporarily grant owner-write permission to owned read-only directories, restoring their original permissions when retained. Dry-run does not change permissions. Empty directories are removed after their eligible files; missing roots are harmless on subsequent runs. Summary/log byte counts are logical file lengths, not physical space reclaimed. Deletion or permission-restoration failures stop pruning and return a nonzero exit status; they are not reported as successful cleanup. Concurrent hostile writers remain a limitation: the final metadata check and unlink cannot be one atomic conditional operation. Automatic Cargo Artifact Pruning `--prune-target-files` is narrower authorization than `--prune-root`: only discovered Cargo targets qualify, and only recognized generated compiler outputs may be removed. It uses the same strict file cutoff, descriptor-relative deletion, exclusions, ownership/mount checks, activity checks and failure reporting as explicit pruning. Recent files, nested source projects, corpus/evidence/receipt/backup directories, and database-bearing fixture subtrees are retained. Database markers protect their entire subtree, including journal/manifest/lock/keyspace files and SQLite sidecars, rather than merely preserving selected extensions. Automatic pruning does not remove empty directories, so retained fixture directory metadata is not discarded. Without this flag, no new per-file cleanup occurs: whole targets containing recent or protected data remain intact. A completely old, safe target can still be removed as a whole; mixed-age or durable-data-bearing targets use the narrower per-file policy when requested. Dry-Run vs Execute Mode Flag Behavior **Dry-run** (default) *(none)* Prints cleanup summaries. **Nothing is deleted.** **Dry-run list** `--list` Prints stale paths plus the summary. **Nothing is deleted.** **Execute** `-e` / `--execute` Removes eligible directories and explicitly authorized old files, then prints summaries. **Execute list** `-e --list` Prints deleted paths plus the summary. Dry-run is the default because accidentally deleting active build caches is expensive.

title: Automation
text:
Automation on Mac and Linux Schedule only a command you have reviewed manually. The examples here run previews. Adding `--execute` changes their authority and must be an intentional local decision. Use the same lock path for scheduled and manual runs. Native command lookup must work in the scheduler's environment; interactive shell startup files may not be loaded. macOS: launchd Create a user LaunchAgent only after replacing every `/Users/YOU` path below with an absolute path for your account. launchd does not expand `$HOME` inside `ProgramArguments`. <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>local.target-reaper.preview</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key><array>
    <string>/Users/YOU/.cargo/bin/target-reaper</string>
    <string>--root</string><string>/Users/YOU/src</string>
    <string>--age-days</string><string>7</string>
    <string>--min-size</string><string>100M</string>
    <string>--list</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key><dict>
    <key>PATH</key><string>/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin</string>
  </dict>
  <key>StartInterval</key><integer>86400</integer>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/Users/YOU/Library/Logs/target-reaper-preview.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/Users/YOU/Library/Logs/target-reaper-preview.err</string>
</dict></plist>
 Adjust the Homebrew prefix on Intel Macs. Save the file as `~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.target-reaper.preview.plist`, validate it, then explicitly load it: plutil -lint "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/local.target-reaper.preview.plist"
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/local.target-reaper.preview.plist"
 To stop the schedule: launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/local.target-reaper.preview.plist"
 Linux: systemd user timer `~/.config/systemd/user/target-reaper-preview.service`: [Unit]
Description=Preview stale Rust build artifacts

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=%h/.cargo/bin/target-reaper --root %h/src --age-days 7 --min-size 100M --list
 `~/.config/systemd/user/target-reaper-preview.timer`: [Unit]
Description=Daily Target Reaper preview

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
 After reviewing the files: systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now target-reaper-preview.timer
systemctl --user status target-reaper-preview.timer
journalctl --user -u target-reaper-preview.service
 To stop it, use `systemctl --user disable --now target-reaper-preview.timer`. Before authorizing scheduled deletion Review the exact roots, age, size, exclusions, lock path and category flags. Confirm that scheduler logs are readable and retained. A daily schedule does not justify `--discard-stale-workspaces` or broad per-file scope. Installing the binary or building these docs does not create any schedule. No cleanup service is enabled by this repository automatically.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Troubleshooting Stable compiler rejects a nightly option An older wrapper always added `-Zallow-features`, even with a stable compiler pin. Update to the compatibility fix and run the wrapper tests. Do not enable `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP` or silently remove the nightly allowlist. rustup show active-toolchain
python3 .cargo/test_strict_rustc.py
 GNU timeout is unavailable Check `timeout --version`. On macOS, Homebrew coreutils supplies `gtimeout` and a `gnubin` directory. Add the correct path to the shell or scheduled job's environment. launchd may not inherit an interactive shell's `PATH`. macOS retains an active or unverified root An open file, current directory or mapped executable may retain an entire pruning root. Required capability snapshots must also be complete. Close only your own completed fixture handles when testing; do not stop services or remove protection checks to force deletion. An inaccessible process or a process starting after the snapshot remains a visibility limit. A snapshot is not an atomic lock on other processes. A worktree remains Inspect the category-specific retained reason and selected policy. Missing registrations require their own opt-in. Old build output does not make an unmerged or recovery-bearing checkout eligible. `--discard-stale-workspaces` authorizes loss of old unfinished data; do not add it merely to suppress a retained reason. JJ version or repository-format mismatch Check the native CLI version, locked JJ library version and repository format. Use fixtures created by supported tools. Unreadable membership/store evidence retains workspaces. Do not rewrite a real store for an unverified build. A build reaches its budget Keep the stopped log and closure receipt. Separate build-cache growth from shared-volume changes before choosing a measured next step. Reusing a cache can reduce demand; do not reset counters or increase an approved cap without the required authorization. Preview differs from execution They capture different live snapshots. Execution can retain changed candidates, or an earlier workspace removal can release a later branch candidate. Preview is not a saved transaction. Review category counters rather than summing overlapping estimates. Physical space differs from reported bytes Logical lengths do not include sparse allocation, compression, shared blocks or external hard links. Measure filesystem availability independently when physical reclamation matters.

title: Architecture
text:
Architecture One policy engine, two native platform implementations. Flow CLI configuration
  → bounded discovery and classification
  → typed eligibility / retention decisions
  → final metadata and process revalidation
  → explicitly authorized native removal
  → category counters and retained reasons
 Discovery supplies facts; eligibility decides what may proceed. Actions own filesystem and repository effects. A scan is not an irrevocable deletion plan. Module map Area Modules Responsibility Orchestration `main`, `config`, `actions` Authorization, shared lock, ordering and reporting Discovery `parallel_walk`, `calc`, `artifacts` Bounded traversal, facts and generated-artifact scope Git facts `native_git`, `worktree_discovery`, `worktree_model` Native library state and typed registrations/revisions Integration authority `repository_base`, `branches`, `branch_model` Pinned main/master basis and branch eligibility JJ state `jj_guard`, `jj_workspace_discovery`, `jj_workspace_discard` Ownership, membership, stores and exact-name operations Removal `cleanup`, `prune`, `prune_fs`, `prune_activity` Final checks, no-follow traversal and explicit deletion OS evidence `platform_fs`, `platform_macos`, `platform_macos_parse` Native handles, activity and mount snapshots Retention/recovery `worktree_missing`, `worktree_generated`, `workspace_activity`, `retention` Private metadata, generated-cache authorization and retained reasons Native repository state Current development uses `gix` and `jj-lib` for native repository facts. Bounded external Git/JJ commands remain where the workflow requires them. CLI and library versions both belong in the verification record. Concurrency and accounting Discovery and review use bounded queues and worker pools. Execution revalidates facts at effect boundaries. Counters separate physical workspaces and logical bytes from registrations and branch operations. Performance claims require measurements for the workload in question. A faster scan is not a stronger atomicity or recoverability guarantee.

title: Development
text:
Development and verification Use an owned disposable checkout and fixture roots. Never point tests or an unverified build at personal repositories, home directories or real cleanup data. Compiler policy `rust-toolchain.toml` pins Rust 1.99.1 with rustfmt, Clippy and LLVM tools. Stable Rust rejects unstable feature attributes. For an explicitly selected nightly/dev compiler, `.cargo/strict-rustc.sh` enforces exactly `portable_simd,try_blocks`, rejects conflicts and covers dependency compiler probes. `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP` is rejected. Toolchain and policy changes are reviewable changes, not dependency workarounds. Fast checks python3 .cargo/test_strict_rustc.py
cargo fmt --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --lib --bins --examples --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
 All-targets checking compiles tests, examples and benches; it does not execute Criterion benchmarks. Strict source linting is separate from test implementation style. Fixture tests Install `cargo-nextest` from its official distribution, then: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --tests \
  --all-features --locked --test-threads 2 --no-fail-fast
 Use isolated `HOME`/`TMPDIR`, isolated VCS config, no network during execution, and writes limited to owned fixtures/build output. Keep foreign jobs intact. Resource supervision must confirm exit/reap and owned descendant closure. Do not walk live fixture candidates to measure space: the monitor's directory descriptors can correctly trigger activity retention. Record owned build-cache growth separately from shared-volume changes, while preserving the shared free-space floor. For constrained builds, disable debug symbols and incremental output without disabling runtime assertions or overflow checks: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 \
  cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --tests --all-features --locked --test-threads 2
 Declare budgets before execution. Stopped or partial runs remain incomplete, and cache reuse does not turn them into passing evidence. Native OS coverage Run Mac fixtures on macOS and Linux fixtures on Linux. Target checks do not validate another kernel's process/filesystem behavior. Do not substitute Docker/VM execution when a task requires an authorized native executor. `test-plan.md`, `test-plan-review.md` and `test-suite-review.md` record broader contracts and historical evidence. Read their commit/scope and blocked cases before interpreting counts. Assurance checks Tools include audit, deny, vet, geiger, machete, feature combinations and scoped mutations. Preserve real exit statuses and output. The checked-in Cargo license policy accepts MIT, Apache-2.0 and Unicode-3.0 for normal/build dependencies. Do not add blanket exemptions or invent audits. Vet imports, publisher attestations and criteria need approved provenance before coverage can be claimed. Mutation inventories are candidates, not execution: require a baseline and classify caught, missed, unviable and interrupted outcomes. Build these docs Python 3.10 or newer is required: python3 -m venv .venv-docs
.venv-docs/bin/pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
.venv-docs/bin/python scripts/build_docs.py --output target/devdocs
.venv-docs/bin/python scripts/check_docs.py target/devdocs
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory target/devdocs
 The public site contains documentation only. It does not make the private source repository or release assets public.

title: Release packages
text:
Mac and Linux packages Build each package on its native OS, validate the exact source commit, then package the binary. Packaging does not run tests and does not certify a release. Platform-specific builds On Apple-silicon macOS: cargo build --release --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin
python3 scripts/package_release.py \
  --binary target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/target-reaper \
  --target aarch64-apple-darwin --output target/packages
 On x86-64 Linux: cargo build --release --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
python3 scripts/package_release.py \
  --binary target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/target-reaper \
  --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --output target/packages
 The packager checks the executable's OS/architecture header, records binary and source fingerprints, and creates an archive plus checksum manifest. Its default label is `development`; use a release label only as part of an actually verified release process. Package contents File Purpose `target-reaper` Native executable for the named target `BUILD.json` Commit, dirty-source state, source fingerprint, binary hash and package target `INSTALL.md` Installation and documentation link `SHA256SUMS` Checksums for packaged files The archive also receives a sidecar `.sha256` checksum. The `packaging_checkout_commit`, `packaging_checkout_dirty` and `packaging_checkout_source_sha256` fields describe the checkout used for packaging. They do not by themselves prove which source produced the supplied binary. `build_binding` defaults to **Unverified**. Passing `--verification-receipt PATH` requires matching source, binary, target and passing native-test evidence, records the receipt/test-log hashes, and labels the relationship as local evidence rather than a signed attestation. An older tag or an artifact uploaded by a workflow must not be presented as a verified current-head build without its native test evidence. Verify before installing On macOS, use `shasum -a 256 ARCHIVE.tar.gz`. On Linux, use `sha256sum ARCHIVE.tar.gz`. Compare the result to the sidecar checksum from the same trusted release. Inspect `BUILD.json` after extraction, confirm the target matches your machine, then install for your user: install -d "$HOME/.local/bin"
install -m 755 target-reaper "$HOME/.local/bin/target-reaper"
"$HOME/.local/bin/target-reaper" --version
 Unsigned development Mac binaries are not notarized applications. A binary that runs on the verification Mac is not automatically certified for all older macOS versions. Distribution boundary The source repository and its release assets are private. Public documentation does not grant download access. No new production release is claimed until the matching Mac and Linux artifacts and required verification actually exist. Prepared native build workflow `.github/workflows/native-versions.yml` targets `macos-15` on ARM64 and `ubuntu-24.04` on x86-64. It uses official checksum-pinned native test tools, a read-only token, one build job and two test threads. It produces development archives only after its native checks pass. Hosted runners are VMs. Where a task forbids VM substitution, obtain explicit approval before using them. The workflow stays gated until a manual dispatch explicitly approves hosted runners, or an authorized same-repository PR receives the `native-runners-approved` label. A skipped job is not a passing verification result. Jobs have a 20-minute outer limit; individual monitored stages stop at 1 GiB sampled owned RSS, 2 GiB build cache, a 4 GiB free-space floor, low available memory or the 15-minute stage watchdog. The build-cache limit counts the full owned cache, not a reset baseline between stages. macOS also uses the native write/network sandbox; Linux uses a dedicated disposable runner with isolated fixture HOME/TMPDIR and VCS configuration. This workflow does not waive vet provenance, dependency policy or other release-assurance obligations. Workflow artifacts are not automatically published as production releases.
